rows.note: D38 sanity: the aurora shader is in the Atmospheres bundle and the renderer started (AuroraRenderer.Ready)
D38 sanity: setting Auto draws the shell where no foreign aurora layer exists (AuroraPolicy)
D38 sanity: setting Auto hands a body with a foreign aurora layer over to it
D38 sanity: the AURORA rule of the body is on (the patch in Atmospheres/Aurora/AtmospheresAurora.cfg switches it on for Kerbin)
D38 informative: the model's activity at the time of the start
D38 informative: 1 where an EVE layer with 'aurora' in its name exists on the body (SPVE, EVEVolumetricsAurorae); Auto then leaves the aurora to it
D38-07: the shell takes body.transform.up as the pole; the largest angle to CelestialBody.RotationAxis over the bodies with an atmosphere (a tilted body shows it)
Start aurora, pose check: the flight camera's compass heading and elevation are within 3 degrees of the pose asked for (otherwise the poses below are not the poses they say)
Start aurora, pose check: the sun elevation at the camera is within 2 degrees of the -12 asked for (-11 at 78 degrees latitude)
Start aurora, premise: Scatterer is loaded (the draw-order rows below are about Scatterer's sky; without it they say nothing about D38-01)
D38-11 informative: the anti-aliasing samples of the quality level during the start (the depth tests were not measured with MSAA before)

Start aurora, D38-01 control: the frame the probe reads changes when the shell is drawn unrestricted (none_after: no depth test, after the transparent range). 0 means the frame source is frozen (RECON: EVE without Scatterer) and every real-sky row below is void

D38-01: the default draw (hardware depth buffer, BeforeForwardAlpha) paints the sky with Scatterer present: peak row mean of the contribution mask at lat 70, activity 1, 25 degrees up, sun -12 at least 0.004. 0 is the first build's failure (every pixel discarded)

D38-01 decision: peak of the default draw (BeforeForwardAlpha) over peak of the same draw at AfterForwardAlpha. Expected below 1 (Scatterer's sky, queue 2998, extinguishes what was drawn before it) and at least 0.25. Below 0.25 the sky removes the aurora: set aurora.event to 1 as the default (the aurora then lies over the sky and the EVE clouds)

D38-01 informative: peak of the unrestricted dome at BeforeForwardAlpha over AfterForwardAlpha. 1 means the sky does not touch the shell at all (then Scatterer's sky draws before BeforeForwardAlpha or is not an extinction); the value says how much the sky takes
D38-01: the share of pixels the hardware test paints over the share the unrestricted dome paints, in an open sky: at least 0.9 (the test must not discard sky)
D38-01 informative: 1 where the far-value test on a copy of BuiltinRenderTextureType.Depth paints anything. 0 reproduces RECON P6 (the copy holds 0.314 in the sky, never the far value)
D38-01 informative: the same for ResolvedDepth
D38-01 informative: the same for the global depth texture
D38-01 informative: peak row mean of the contribution mask, hardware depth test, BeforeForwardAlpha
D38-01 informative: hardware depth test, AfterForwardAlpha
D38-01 informative: no depth test, BeforeForwardAlpha
D38-01 informative: no depth test, AfterForwardAlpha
D38-01 informative: far-value test on a copy of Depth
D38-01 informative: far-value test on a copy of ResolvedDepth
D38-01 informative: far-value test on a copy of the global depth texture
D38-01 control of the occlusion rows: without the opaque ball the square where the ball will stand is lit by the shell (mean mask at least 0.001)
D38-01 negative control: the unrestricted dome paints over the opaque ball (mean mask in the ball's square at least 0.001), so the ball is seen by the test and not by the picture

D38-01: an opaque ball in front of the brightest part of the shell hides it with the default test (mean mask in the ball's inner square at most 0.0001): terrain, vessels and mountains occlude the aurora in the real frame
D38-01 informative: the same for the far-value test on a copy of Depth
D38-01 informative: the same for ResolvedDepth
D38-01 informative: the same for the global depth texture

D38-01 informative: the same for the global depth texture tested against the sky value RECON P6 measured (0.314, tolerance 0.03) instead of the far value; the candidate for the default when the hardware test does not hide the ball
D38-01 informative: the sky-value test on the global depth texture paints the sky (peak at least 0.004)
D38-01 informative: peak row mean with the sky-value test on the global depth texture, BeforeForwardAlpha
Start aurora, premise: the AURORA rule of the body is on in the climate the renderer reads (otherwise the shell never draws and the probe stops before any frame row)

D38-02, real sky: the largest step between adjacent row means of the contribution mask over the peak row mean, worst over the judged poses (lat 60 with the strong event, 70, 78; activity 1 and 0.6; aimed at the middle of the curtain; and 20 degrees lower at lat 78 and 15 degrees higher at lat 70; sun -12; the mask leaves out pixels brighter than 0.45 so that discs and flames do not count), default draw, Scatterer, EVE, TUFX and Parallax present. The earlier layer's artefact was a hard lid
D38-02, real sky: the share of lit columns whose lowest lit row hangs more than 6 % of the picture below the median of its neighbours, worst over the judged poses
D38-02, real sky: the mean contribution below 3 degrees of view elevation over the peak row mean, worst over the judged poses

D38-02/D38-05: poses of the eight bright enough to judge (peak row mean at least 0.004); the others are counted in D38.sky.poses_dim, so that a worst value of zero cannot come from dropping everything
D38-05 informative: poses that were too dim to judge

D38-05: poses the vessel could not be placed at (the game held it back; the log names its state per attempt); a pose left out this way no longer ends the start, so it is counted here and fails the row
D38-05 informative: poses skipped because the latitude has no night at the date (the lowest sun above -6 degrees after the 1 degree margin); each is named in D38.sky.skipped_lowest_sun_deg.<pose>
D38-05: judged + dim + skipped + unplaced is the eight poses of the list, so that none is dropped without a count

D38-02 control: peak row mean of the positive difference of two shell-off frames of the same pose (water, clouds and the sky's own animation) with the pixels of objects (above luminance 0.45: discs, a vessel's flame) left out, worst over every condition of the start (the log line names where the worst came from); under a tenth of the judging level 0.004, else the masks above carry that noise. K-W3 repeat read 0.417 with a rocket's flame in the frame

informative: how much of the curtain the top and bottom two rows of the frame cut (mean mask there over the peak row mean, worst over the judged poses); near 1 the curtain meets the frame edge and the pose is a framing, not a lid test
informative: 1 where the camera's target did not follow the shell and the screen was read instead

D38-03 informative: mean frame time with the shell minus without at the dearest pose (lat 60 with the strong event, 10 degrees up); the whole game frame, so not the GPU figure; the GPU figure is the player's exclusive timing

player stage scene (series aurora): the worst lid step over the grid of 35 poses (sun -6/-12/-25 x activity 0.2/0.6/1.0 x latitude 60/70/78 at 25 degrees; 10 and 40 degrees at sun -12, activity 0.6; and the two strong-event poses at latitude 60)
player stage scene: the worst share of dripping columns over the grid
player stage scene: the worst horizon band share (rows below 3 degrees of elevation) over the grid
player stage scene: poses bright enough to judge (peak row mean at least 0.004); the others are listed as poses.dim and dim.<pose>
player stage scene: a body in front of the view hides the shell (inside <= 1e-4, outside >= 1e-3)
player stage scene: the same state twice gives the same picture (no jitter, no shimmer)
player stage scene: the shell at sun +10 changes nothing

player stage scene (series aurora-time, exclusive): four times the GPU difference of the shell against the mean of the two shell-off runs around it, at 1280 x 720, at a dear pose (activity 1, latitude 78, 10 degrees up, sun -12), 15 rounds of off, on, off; a negative difference counts as zero
player stage scene: the method's own noise, four times the difference of the two shell-off means; at or under the limit, so that the figure above can resolve it
OPEN (owner E40, proxy run): trail pixels of the shell under DLSS K/M/L, FSR 3 and XeSS against the baseline + 20 %, RT on and off
OPEN: the volumetric variant (an EVE layer through the C23 binding) is not built; its three discriminators (lower step size, camera ground vs 10 km, raised minimum altitude) wait for it
